title: Taylor Hawkins - Wikipedia
notes: Oliver Taylor Hawkins, born 17 February 1972, Fort Worth, Texas; to Laguna Beach, California, in 1976; Laguna Beach High School 1990. Sylvia; Sass Jordan; Alanis Morissette's drummer from June 1995 to March 1997 (Jagged Little Pill, Live). Joined Foo Fighters, announced 18 March 1997, after The Colour and the Shape, on which Grohl played; eight studio albums with them, There Is Nothing Left to Lose to Medicine at Midnight; a co-writer on every one. Sang Have a Cigar, Cold Day in the Sun, Sunday Rain, Somebody to Love live. Guns N' Roses asked him in 2000; Roger Taylor talked him into staying. The Coattail Riders (2006, 2010, 2019), Chevy Metal, the Birds of Satan, NHC; drums on Coheed and Cambria's No World for Tomorrow (2007). Rhythm's Best Rock Drummer, 2005; Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, 2021. Influences: Phil Collins, Stewart Copeland ('whom he idolized and eventually befriended'), Budgie, Roger Taylor, Stephen Perkins, Jim Gordon, Neil Peart, Alex Van Halen, John Bonham. 'Hawkins's first two major inspirations were Roger Taylor and Stewart Copeland'; he played along to records such as Queen's News of the World. Ludwig, Tama, then Gretsch from 2005; Zildjian cymbals. Died 25 March 2022, Bogotá. Tribute concerts at Wembley (3 September) and the Kia Forum (27 September 2022); his son Shane played My Hero.

title: Taylor Hawkins, hard-driving but humble, reached drumming greatness with a smile
notes: Daniel Arkin, NBC News, 27 March 2022. Hawkins to Rolling Stone: 'If he is the disciple of [Led Zeppelin drummer] John Bonham, I'm a disciple of Stewart Copeland. I mean, that is really kind of the easiest way of putting it.' To the AP (2009): Phil Collins 'one of my favorite drummers ever'. Jordan Runtagh: 'He was the engine behind it all.'

title: PAS Playlist: Taylor Hawkins
notes: Nick Costa, Percussive Arts Society, 18 October 2022. 'Combining elements of Neil Peart, Roger Taylor, Phil Collins, Stewart Copeland, and Ringo Starr.' Times Like These 'starts out with an eighth-note driven hi-hat groove as the band alternates between measures of 4/4 and 3/4'. Rope: 'driving eighth-note grooves throughout the verses' and 'a chorus groove paying homage to Neil Peart'. Run: he adapts 'a soca beat' for most of the song, ride and crash grooves in the chorus. DOA: 'a tom-driven groove'. Aurora: 'segments of driving grooves, solid fills, and even drum breaks'.

title: Greatest Hits (Foo Fighters album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 3 November 2009. Personnel: Grohl drums on tracks 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 12 (Everlong, My Hero, Learn to Fly, Monkey Wrench, Big Me, This Is a Call); Hawkins on the rest, Breakout among them. Wheels and Word Forward new, with Butch Vig.

title: Foo Fighters, Live at Wembley Stadium (2008): All My Life and Times Like These, the band's official uploads
notes: Filmed at Wembley Stadium, London, 6 and 7 June 2008; released on DVD in August 2008. All My Life (aiy5W3z4SGE), Hawkins at the kit 0:38-0:50; Times Like These (cvCUXXsP5WE), 0:05, 0:35, 2:31-2:51. Long, straight, middle-parted sandy-blond hair past the shoulders, a full beard, a black sleeveless shirt, a black Gretsch kit with chrome hardware, a white front head with the Gretsch script, brilliant Zildjian cymbals, no headphones.

title: There Is Nothing Left to Lose - Wikipedia
notes: Released 2 November 1999, Roswell/RCA. Recorded in Grohl's basement in Alexandria, Virginia, with Adam Kasper. 'The album is the first to feature Hawkins on drums. He performed on the majority of album, while leaving the faster songs for Grohl to play. The liner notes of the album do not specify who plays on which songs, although Hawkins states "Aurora" and "M.I.A." are good examples of his playing style, and that he plays the "jazzier" drums parts.'

title: One by One (Foo Fighters album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 22 October 2002. The first sessions (Virginia, then Conway, Los Angeles) discarded as 'million-dollar demos' (Hawkins); re-recorded in two weeks at Studio 606, Grohl visiting Hawkins in Topanga to rework the songs; Nick Raskulinecz promoted to producer. All My Life the lead single (September 2002), Grammy for Best Hard Rock Performance; Times Like These, Low and Have It All singles in 2003.

title: In Your Honor - Wikipedia
notes: Released 14 June 2005, a double album, heavy and acoustic. Recorded January to March 2005 at Studio 606 West, Northridge, with Nick Raskulinecz. Best of You the lead single (30 May 2005), the band's highest-charting; DOA in August. Hawkins drums; Grohl drums on Cold Day in the Sun, which Hawkins sings.

title: Echoes, Silence, Patience & Grace - Wikipedia
notes: Released 25 September 2007. Recorded from March 2007 at Studio 606 with Gil Norton; Grohl's demos first developed with Hawkins. The Pretender the lead single (August 2007), Long Road to Ruin the second. Hawkins: drums, background vocals, piano on Summer's End.

title: Wasting Light - Wikipedia
notes: Released 12 April 2011. Recorded to tape from 6 September 2010 in Grohl's garage in Encino with Butch Vig, a carpet under the kit to make it 'less loud and bright', the crash traded to cut the bleed. 'The recordings started with Grohl's rhythm guitar and Taylor Hawkins' drumming to provide the foundations and see if both could "lock in". Hawkins usually played for hours before he got "a drum track I'd be proud of".' Click tracks, but Vig 'wanted it to groove'. Rope the lead single, then Walk, Arlandria, These Days, Bridge Burning.

title: Concrete and Gold - Wikipedia
notes: Released 15 September 2017. Recorded at EastWest Studios with Greg Kurstin. Run the lead single (June 2017, number one on the Mainstream Rock chart). Hawkins drums on all but track 9, Sunday Rain, which he sings and Paul McCartney drums.
